settings.heading: What is Fladrafinil?
settings.definition: Fladrafinil (CRL-40,941) is a eugeroic, or wakefulness-promoting, research compound. It is the bisfluoro structural analog of adrafinil, which is itself a prodrug of modafinil. People reach for it to support sustained alertness and focus during demanding days, without the jittery overstimulation of high-dose caffeine.
settings.scientific_body:
Class: eugeroic; part of the adrafinil/modafinil family developed at Lafon Laboratories. Fladrafinil is thought to influence dopamine and orexin signaling, systems tied to wakefulness and motivation. Onset is typically 30–60 minutes with effects lasting roughly 6–8 hours; timing and response vary by individual and dose.

  • Structure: bisfluoroadrafinil analog of adrafinil.
  • Rationale: smoother, non-amphetamine wakefulness for long focus blocks.
  • Forms: pre-measured 20 mg capsules, or powder for users who prefer to weigh their own servings.

Fladrafinil is an unapproved research compound with very limited human data. Informational only. Not medical advice.
